arxiv-2108-13801.title: Optimal Latency-Oriented Coding and Scheduling in Parallel Queuing Systems
arxiv-2108-13801.creator: Andrea Bedin, Federico Chiariotti, Stepan Kucera, Andrea Zanella
arxiv-2108-13801.description: Abstract The evolution of 5G and Beyond networks has enabled new applications with stringent end-to-end latency requirements, but providing reliable low-latency service with high throughput over public wireless networks is still a significant challenge. One of the possible ways to solve this is to exploit path diversity, encoding the information flow over multiple streams across parallel links.

arxiv-2207-04038.title: Contact Lie systems: theory and applications Thanks: e-mail: javier.de.lucas@fuw.edu.pl ORCID: 0000-0001-8643-144X Thanks: e-mail: xavier.rivas@unir.net ORCID: 0000-0002-4175-5157
arxiv-2207-04038.creator: [2ex] UW Institute for Advanced StudiesDepartment of Mathematical Methods in Physics, University of Warsaw, Warszawa, Poland., [1ex] Escuela Superior de Ingeniería y TecnologíaUniversidad Internacional de La Rioja, Logroño, Spain.[1ex]
arxiv-2207-04038.description: Abstract We define and analyse the properties of contact Lie systems, namely systems of first-order differential equations describing the integral curves of a t t -dependent vector field taking values in a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of Hamiltonian vector fields relative to a contact manifold. All contact automorphic Lie systems associated with left-invariant contact forms on three-dimensional Lie groups are classified.

arxiv-2302-02924.title: Dropout Injection at Test Time for Post Hoc Uncertainty Quantification in Neural Networks Journal: Information Sciences
arxiv-2302-02924.creator: Emanuele Ledda, Giorgio Fumera, Fabio Roli
arxiv-2302-02924.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Emanuele Ledda, Giorgio Fumera, Fabio Roli. Among Bayesian methods, Monte-Carlo dropout provides principled tools for evaluating the epistemic uncertainty of neural networks. Its popularity recently led to seminal works that proposed activating the dropout layers only during inference for evaluating uncertainty.

arxiv-2308-13713.title: Causally Sound Priors for Binary Experiments

arxiv-2308-13713.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nicholas J. Irons, Carlos Cinelli. We introduce the BREASE framework for the Bayesian analysis of randomized controlled trials with a binary treatment and a binary outcome. Approaching the problem from a causal inference perspective, we propose parameterizing the likelihood in terms of the b aseline r isk, e fficacy, and a dverse s ide e ffects of the treatment, along with a flexible, yet intuitive and tractable jointly independent beta prior distribution on these parameters, which we show to be a generalization of the

arxiv-2407-01448.title: Iwahori Spherical Whittaker Functions for Steinberg Representations
arxiv-2407-01448.creator: Ehud Moshe Baruch, Markos Karameris
arxiv-2407-01448.description: Abstract Let G G be a split reductive group over a p p -adic field F F and let ( π S ​ t , V ) (\pi_{St},V) be a Steinberg representation of G G with trivial central character. It is known that the space of Iwahori fixed vectors in V V is one-dimensional.

arxiv-2408-14221.title: Brain functions emerge as thermal equilibrium states of the connectome
arxiv-2408-14221.creator: Elkaïoum M. Moutuou, Habib Benali
arxiv-2408-14221.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Elkaïoum M. Moutuou, Habib Benali. A fundamental paradigm in neuroscience is that cognitive functions—such as perception, learning, memory, and locomotion—are shaped by the brain’s structural organization. However, the theoretical principles explaining how this physical architecture governs its function remain elusive. Here, we propose an algebraic quantum mechanics (AQM) framework in which the functional states of a structural connectome emerge as thermal equilibrium states of an algebraic quantum system defined on the underlying directed multigraph.

arxiv-2505-22387.title: DAM: Domain-Aware Module for Multi-Domain Dataset Condensation
arxiv-2505-22387.creator: Jaehyun Choi, Gyojin Han, Dong-Jae Lee, Sunghyun Baek, Junmo Kim
arxiv-2505-22387.description: Abstract Dataset Condensation (DC) has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate the computational and storage burdens associated with training deep learning models. However, existing DC methods largely overlook the multi-domain nature of modern datasets, which are increasingly composed of heterogeneous images spanning multiple domains.

arxiv-2511-09196.title: Genuine and spurious bistability in a simple epidemic model with waning immunity
arxiv-2511-09196.creator: Francesca Scarabel, Harry Coldwell, Tyler Cassidy
arxiv-2511-09196.description: Abstract We study an infection-age structured epidemic model in which both the infectivity and the rate of loss of immunity depend on the time-since-infection. The model can be equivalently viewed as a nonlinear renewal equation for the incidence of infection or as a partial differential equation for the density of infected individuals.

arxiv-2512-05199.title: Jet Charge with Global Event Shapes: Probing Quark Flavor Dynamics
arxiv-2512-05199.creator: Yang-Ting Chien, Sonny Mantry
arxiv-2512-05199.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yang-Ting Chien, Sonny Mantry. We propose measuring the jet electric charge of jet regions, defined within the framework of global event shapes, as a probe of quark flavor dynamics within the nucleon and the hadronization process. In particular, we consider a measurement of the jet region charge while simultaneously keeping track of the energy flow throughout the event, as characterized by the global event shape.

europmc-pmc4271684.creator: Oza S, Lawn JE, Hogan DR, Mathers C, Cousens SN.
europmc-pmc4271684.description: Objective To estimate cause-of-death distributions in the early (0-6 days of age) and late (7-27 days of age) neonatal periods, for 194 countries between 2000 and 2013. Methods For 65 countries with high-quality vital registration, we used each country's observed early and late

plos-pone-0002132.title: Antimalarial Drug Quality in the Most Severely Malarious Parts of Africa – A Six Country Study
plos-pone-0002132.creator: Roger Bate, Philip Coticelli, Richard Tren et al.
plos-pone-0002132.description: PLOS ONE research article. A range of antimalarial drugs were procured from private pharmacies in urban and peri-urban areas in the major cities of six African countries, situated in the part of that continent and the world that is most highly endemic for malaria. Semi-quantitative thin-layer chromatograph

plos-pone-0010566.creator: Takashi Shimbo, Atsushi Tanemura, Takehiko Yamazaki et al.
plos-pone-0010566.description: PLOS ONE research article. Malignant melanoma is one of the most aggressive types of tumor. Because malignant melanoma is difficult to treat once it has metastasized, early detection and treatment are essential. The search for reliable biomarkers of early-stage melanoma, therefore, has received much attent

pmc-10510103.title: Structure-Based Design of Small Imine Reductase Panels for Target Substrates
pmc-10510103.creator: Yuqi Yu, Arnau Rué Casamajo, William Finnigan, Christian Schnepel, Rhys Barker, Charlotte Morrill, Rachel S. Heath, Leonardo De Maria, Nicholas J. Turner, Nigel S. Scrutton
pmc-10510103.description: Biocatalysis is important in the discovery, development, and manufacture of pharmaceuticals. However, the identification of enzymes for target transformations of interest requires major screening efforts. Here, we report a structure-based computational workflow to prioritize protein sequences by a score based on predicted activities on substrates, thereby reducing a resource-intensive laboratory-based biocatalyst screening.

pmc-11439409.title: Diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma: Molecular and clinical insights in managing metastatic disease
pmc-11439409.creator: Nathaniel Grabill, Mena Louis, Mariah Cawthon, Claudia Gherasim, James Chambers
pmc-11439409.description: Adenosquamous carcinoma of the pancreas (ASCP) is a rare and aggressive variant of pancreatic cancer, characterized by both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma components. It presents significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to its atypical histology and poor prognosis. A 72-year-old male presented with abdominal pain, lighter-colored stools, and intermittent nausea.

pmc-11452820.title: Online Medication Abortion Direct-to-Patient Fulfillment Before and After the Dobbs v Jackson Decision
pmc-11452820.creator: Caila Brander, Jessica Nouhavandi, Terri-Ann Thompson
pmc-11452820.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Key PointsQuestionHow did prescription fulfilment for direct-to-patient medication abortion provision change for 1 online pharmacy after the Dobbs v Jackson Women’s Health Organization decision, considering patient, prescriber, and state policy characteristics?FindingsIn this cross-sectional study including 87 942 fulfilled prescriptions, there was an overall increase in prescription fulfilment for direct-to-patient medication abortions in the year after the Dobbs v Jackson decision compared with the year prior, with spikes in prescription fulfillment following the Dobbs v Jackson leak and the Dobbs v Jackson decision

pmc-12629702.title: A Review of Novel Cancer Therapeutics and Current Research Trends
pmc-12629702.creator: Abimbola Mary Oluwajembola, Suleiman Zakari, Wisdom D. Cleanclay, Timothy Ayeni, Adewale Adebosoye, Olayinka S. Okoh, Joshua Folamade, Inalegwu Bawa, Olubanke Olujoke Ogunlana
pmc-12629702.description: The unchecked growth and spread of aberrant cells describe a widely diverse collection of disorders that collectively constitute cancer. Conventional therapies for cancer, including radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and surgery, have increased the chances of survival significantly in most patients. These traditional methods usually result in low tumor or tumor cell specificity, significant systemic toxicity, and the development of drug resistance.

pmc-12669399.title: Imputation of incomplete ordinal and nominal data by predictive mean matching
pmc-12669399.creator: Peter C Austin, Stef van Buuren
pmc-12669399.description: Multivariate imputation using chained equations is a popular algorithm for imputing missing data that entails specifying multivariable models through conditional distributions. Two standard imputation methods for imputing missing continuous variables are parametric imputation using a linear model and predictive mean matching.

pmc-12801706.title: Retrobulbar haemorrhage post sub-Tenons block: a case report
pmc-12801706.creator: Alessandro M Costa, Sharanjeet Sidhu, Thomas G Hardy
pmc-12801706.description: BackgroundRetrobulbar hemorrhage is a rare, sight-threatening complication from trauma, orbital surgery, and, rarely, regional orbital anesthetic injections. This may lead to orbital compartment syndrome with vascular and neural compromise and subsequent irreversible vision loss if not addressed promptly. Retrobulbar hemorrhage following sub-Tenon’s anesthetic is very rare, typically occurring in patients with an increased risk of bleeding from various causes.

pmc-12933797.title: Generative artificial intelligence in dementia care: a scoping review protocol on nursing roles, experiences and ethical perspectives
pmc-12933797.creator: Yong-Chuan Chen, Hsiao-Chi Nieh, Hsiao-Chu Chen, Jung-Chih Chen, Mei-Yu Chang, Pi-O Wu
pmc-12933797.description: AbstractIntroductionGenerative artificial intelligence (GAI), including large language models and multimodal generative systems, is rapidly emerging in healthcare with growing interest in its potential applications for dementia care. These technologies offer new possibilities for communication support, cognitive engagement and personalised interaction, yet they also introduce complex ethical, relational and practical challenges.

pmc-13041291.title: SASdb: a comprehensive database for sex-biased alternative splicing profiles in human tissues
pmc-13041291.creator: Xi Chen, Yueqi Lu, You Duan, Yongfeng Bai, Weidong Ye, Sijia Chen, Hang Zhou, Heng Xu, Le Xu, Cheng Guo
pmc-13041291.description: Alternative splicing (AS) significantly enhances transcriptomic diversity, and its dysregulation is implicated in numerous human diseases. However, no public database systematically compiles sex-related AS events across human tissues. We developed SASdb (http://www.gdbioinfo.top/sasdb), a comprehensive database contains 2,951,059 AS events and 46,418 sex-biased alternative splicing (SAS) events, covering 22 human tissues.

pmc-13180141.title: Long-term lung function decline from chronic workplace exposure in roadside vendors of Peshawar, Pakistan
pmc-13180141.creator: Hamza Khan Khattak, Zmarak Ahmed Khan, Saadia Ashraf, Mahliqa Kirmani, Laiba Malik, Kainat Usman, Syed Abdullah, Kamil Ahmad Kamil, Bushra Iftikhar
pmc-13180141.description: BackgroundAir pollution is a leading global public health challenge, with PM2.5 exposure strongly associated with respiratory and cardiovascular morbidity. In developing countries like Pakistan, urban air pollution levels are particularly severe. In 2021, Peshawar was ranked 9th globally for pollution, with PM2.5 levels 12 to 16 times higher than WHO limits.

pmc-13185450.title: Purifying selection during maternal inheritance of mammalian mtDNA depends on autophagy and bottleneck size
pmc-13185450.creator: Polyxeni Papadea, Nils-Göran Larsson
pmc-13185450.description: Mammalian mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is transmitted asexually without recombination and accumulates mutations at a high rate, which eventually should cause a mutational meltdown. Two processes operating in the maternal germline, the genetic bottleneck and purifying selection, are counteracting this decline but the exact molecular mechanisms and their possible link remain incompletely understood.

pmc-13336065.title: Longitudinal changes in DTI‐ALPS and choroid plexus volume relative to CSF biomarkers during lecanemab treatment in mild cognitive impairment: A pilot study
pmc-13336065.creator: Toshiya Takahashi, Kaku Kimura, Shingo Takenaka, Sayaka Ono, Maya Fukui, Yasushi Okada, Tomohiko Asada, Kan Niimi, Akio Ikeda, Ryosuke Takahashi, Riki Matsumoto, Hidenao Fukuyama
pmc-13336065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BACKGROUNDLecanemab improves cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers, but whether magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) proxies of CSF–interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange improve is unknown.METHODSThis was a single‐center prospective pilot (n = 8). The ALPS index was derived from diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI‐ALPS), and intracranial volume (ICV)–normalized choroid plexus (ChP) volume was segmented with FreeSurfer Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG).

pmc-13460892.title: Health policies and reforms in Mexico (2000-2024): segmentation and challenges for universal rights
pmc-13460892.creator: Eduarda Ferreira dos Anjos, Oliva López-Arellano, Elzo Pereira Pinto, Cristiani Vieira Machado, Eduarda Ferreira dos Anjos, Oliva López-Arellano, Elzo Pereira Pinto, Cristiani Vieira Machado
pmc-13460892.description: The Mexican health system is historically segmented, being based on social insurance for formal workers and public health actions for the general population. This study characterizes health reforms in Mexico from 2000 to 2024 considering the trajectory of health policies, coverage, and use of the health system.

pmc-13559352.title: Forecasting the risk of early death among patients suffering from lung cancer with brain metastasis after radiotherapy using interpretable machine learning: a study based on the SEER database
pmc-13559352.creator: Ruopiao Song, Zhijun Zhang, Xiaoou Huo, Chenhui Qin, Junyan Cao, Shumin Zhang
pmc-13559352.description: BackgroundLung cancer with brain metastasis (LCBM) significantly shortens patient survival. Accurately predicting individual prognosis remains challenging. This study aimed to identify key prognostic factors in LCBM patients after radiotherapy for the development of an interpretable machine learning (ML) model to support clinical decision-making and precision medicine.MethodsBased on clinicopathological data from the U.S.

pmc-13601882.title: Vocal display rules in everyday life: when is it appropriate to laugh, sigh or scream?
pmc-13601882.creator: Roza G Kamiloğlu
pmc-13601882.description: The appropriateness of common nonverbal vocalizations is guided by social norms, known as display rules. This preregistered, 7-day experience-sampling study examined how perceived appropriateness varies across situations. A total of 142 adults completed three surveys per day (2670 surveys total; 3821 vocalizations), rating appropriateness alongside situational cues and psychological situation characteristics.
